title: Slurm node grid - grouping and layout
description: One set of nodes, four ways of deciding what a group is. Same CSV in every panel, so the only difference you are looking at is the grouping key and the layout.

panels.title: By a label, in rack layout
panels.description: The best case: the exporter already publishes the structure. Rack layout stacks each group as a chassis instead of wrapping it. The rack column in this CSV is hand-written: slurm_exporter publishes no such label, and there is nowhere for one to come from because it reads sinfo. Grouping by a label is only available if you add the label yourself, through Prometheus relabelling or a join against an inventory.

panels.title: By a capture on the node name
panels.description: What a real cluster needs. slurm_exporter publishes no rack label - only node, partition, status, instance and job - so the only structure available is the one encoded in the name. '^([a-z]+)' splits c* from g*.

panels.title: By a chunk of the ordinal
panels.description: The fallback when the name carries no structure either. This is the one grouping that asserts something the data never said - it assumes the numbering follows the floor - so the panel marks the groups as assumed.
